entry_conditions.expression: Every bar, place a fixed-direction UP prediction. Stake = current_stake.

exit_conditions.expression: Trade settles on the next bar's close. Win if next_close > entry_close, else lose.

position_sizing_rule: Start at $1. Double after every loss; reset to $1 after every win (martingale).
stop_loss_rule: Session-level: stop trading if cumulative drawdown exceeds $200.
session_filters: Single continuous session (no day-of-week or hour filters specified).
risk_controls: Hard cap: stop session if drawdown > $200.
Hard cap: stop session after 50 trades.

explicit_ambiguities.ambiguity: Payout assumption is not stated. Real Vol75 binary contracts pay roughly 0.95x stake on a win.
explicit_ambiguities.impact_if_different: A realistic 0.95x payout would erode expectancy further and accelerate ruin.

explicit_ambiguities.ambiguity: 'Tick' is undefined. Real Vol75 ticks every 2 seconds; the description also mentions '1min'.
explicit_ambiguities.assumption_used_for_backtest: Treat each 1-minute bar as one trade; outcome is sign of next-bar close minus current close.
explicit_ambiguities.impact_if_different: Higher tick frequency packs more trades per session and brings the cumulative-loss-streak event horizon closer.

explicit_ambiguities.ambiguity: Drawdown definition: peak-to-trough on equity, or session-cumulative loss?
explicit_ambiguities.assumption_used_for_backtest: Session-cumulative PnL falling below -$200 triggers the stop.
explicit_ambiguities.impact_if_different: Peak-to-trough drawdown would trip the stop sooner if the session had any winning streak before the eventual losing run.

explicit_ambiguities.ambiguity: What counts toward the 50-trade cap — entries placed or trades fully settled?
explicit_ambiguities.impact_if_different: Counting placements would change the off-by-one boundary at the cap but not the qualitative outcome.

explicit_ambiguities.ambiguity: 'Predict UP' tie-break: is next_close == current_close a win or a loss?
explicit_ambiguities.assumption_used_for_backtest: Tie counts as a loss (strict greater-than for a win).
explicit_ambiguities.impact_if_different: Counting ties as wins would slightly improve the empirical win-rate but doesn't change the ruin geometry.
